speaker: the swan
devanagari:
दुःशासनस्तूपहन्ता न शास्ता
नावर्तते मन्युवशात्कृतघ्नः ।
न कस्य चिन्मित्रमथो दुरात्मा
कलाश्चैता अधमस्येह पुंसः ॥
iast:
duḥśāsanastūpahantā na śāstā
nāvartate manyuvaśātkṛtaghnaḥ |
na kasya cinmitramatho durātmā
kalāścaitā adhamasyeha puṃsaḥ ||
english: Harsh in command, a destroyer rather than a guide, not turning back from anger, ungrateful, friend to no one, evil-minded: these are the marks of the lowest person here.

speaker: the swan
devanagari:
न श्रद्दधाति कल्याणं परेभ्योऽप्यात्मशङ्कितः ।
निराकरोति मित्राणि यो वै सोऽधम पूरुषः ॥
iast:
na śraddadhāti kalyāṇaṃ parebhyo'pyātmaśaṅkitaḥ |
nirākaroti mitrāṇi yo vai so'dhama pūruṣaḥ ||
english: One who, doubting himself, does not believe any good of others, and drives away his friends, is the lowest person.

speaker: the swan
devanagari:
उत्तमानेव सेवेत प्राप्ते काले तु मध्यमान् ।
अधमांस्तु न सेवेत य इच्छेच्छ्रेय आत्मनः ॥
iast:
uttamāneva seveta prāpte kāle tu madhyamān |
adhamāṃstu na seveta ya icchecchreya ātmanaḥ ||
english: One who wishes his own good should serve the best; when the time comes, the middling; but should not serve the lowest.

speaker: the swan
devanagari:
प्राप्नोति वै वित्तमसद्बलेन
नित्योत्थानात्प्रज्ञया पौरुषेण ।
न त्वेव सम्यग्लभते प्रशंसां
न वृत्तमाप्नोति महाकुलानाम् ॥
iast:
prāpnoti vai vittamasadbalena
nityotthānātprajñayā pauruṣeṇa |
na tveva samyaglabhate praśaṃsāṃ
na vṛttamāpnoti mahākulānām ||
english: One may gain wealth by wicked force, by constant effort, by intelligence and by valour; but one does not truly gain praise, nor the conduct of great families.

speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
महाकुलानां स्पृहयन्ति देवा
धर्मार्थवृद्धाश्च बहुश्रुताश् च ।
पृच्छामि त्वां विदुर प्रश्नमेतं
भवन्ति वै कानि महाकुलानि ॥
iast:
mahākulānāṃ spṛhayanti devā
dharmārthavṛddhāśca bahuśrutāś ca |
pṛcchāmi tvāṃ vidura praśnametaṃ
bhavanti vai kāni mahākulāni ||
english: The gods, those grown in dharma and true benefit, and the deeply learned admire great families. I ask you this question, Vidura: which families are truly great?

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
तमो दमो ब्रह्मवित्त्वं वितानाः
पुण्या विवाहाः सततान्न दानम् ।
येष्वेवैते सप्तगुणा भवन्ति
सम्यग्वृत्तास्तानि महाकुलानि ॥
iast:
tamo damo brahmavittvaṃ vitānāḥ
puṇyā vivāhāḥ satatānna dānam |
yeṣvevaite saptaguṇā bhavanti
samyagvṛttāstāni mahākulāni ||
english: Austerity, self-control, knowledge of the Veda, sacrifices, pure marriages and constant giving of food: families in which these seven qualities are found and practised rightly are great families.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
येषां न वृत्तं व्यथते न योनिर्
वृत्तप्रसादेन चरन्ति धर्मम् ।
ये कीर्तिमिच्छन्ति कुले विशिष्टां
त्यक्तानृतास्तानि महाकुलानि ॥
iast:
yeṣāṃ na vṛttaṃ vyathate na yonir
vṛttaprasādena caranti dharmam |
ye kīrtimicchanti kule viśiṣṭāṃ
tyaktānṛtāstāni mahākulāni ||
english: Those whose conduct does not falter, who do not shame their ancestry, who practise dharma with a glad heart, who wish for distinguished fame for their family and have given up falsehood: those are great families.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अनिज्ययाविवाहैर्श्च वेदस्योत्सादनेन च ।
कुलान्यकुलतां यान्ति धर्मस्यातिक्रमेण च ॥
iast:
anijyayāvivāhairśca vedasyotsādanena ca |
kulānyakulatāṃ yānti dharmasyātikrameṇa ca ||
english: Through neglecting sacrifice, through improper marriages, through abandoning the Veda, and through transgressing dharma, families fall to low standing.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
देव द्रव्यविनाशेन ब्रह्म स्वहरणेन च ।
कुलान्यकुलतां यान्ति ब्राह्मणातिक्रमेण च ॥
iast:
deva dravyavināśena brahma svaharaṇena ca |
kulānyakulatāṃ yānti brāhmaṇātikrameṇa ca ||
english: Through destroying what belongs to the gods, stealing brahmins' property, and slighting brahmins, families fall to low standing.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
ब्राह्मणानां परिभवात्परिवादाच्च भारत ।
कुलान्यकुलतां यान्ति न्यासापहरणेन च ॥
iast:
brāhmaṇānāṃ paribhavātparivādācca bhārata |
kulānyakulatāṃ yānti nyāsāpaharaṇena ca ||
english: Through contempt for brahmins and slander of them, Bharata, and through stealing deposits held in trust, families fall to low standing.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
कुलानि समुपेतानि गोभिः पुरुषतोऽश्वतः ।
कुलसङ्ख्यां न गच्छन्ति यानि हीनानि वृत्ततः ॥
iast:
kulāni samupetāni gobhiḥ puruṣato'śvataḥ |
kulasaṅkhyāṃ na gacchanti yāni hīnāni vṛttataḥ ||
english: Families rich in cattle, people and horses do not count as families if they are lacking in conduct.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
वृत्ततस्त्वविहीनानि कुलान्यल्पधनान्यपि ।
कुलसङ्ख्यां तु गच्छन्ति कर्षन्ति च मयद्यशः ॥
iast:
vṛttatastvavihīnāni kulānyalpadhanānyapi |
kulasaṅkhyāṃ tu gacchanti karṣanti ca mayadyaśaḥ ||
english: But families not lacking in conduct, even if poor in wealth, count as families and win great fame.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
मा नः कुले वैरकृत्कश् चिदस्तु
राजामात्यो मा परस्वापहारी ।
मित्रद्रोही नैकृतिकोऽनृती वा
पूर्वाशी वा पितृदेवातिथिभ्यः ॥
iast:
mā naḥ kule vairakṛtkaś cidastu
rājāmātyo mā parasvāpahārī |
mitradrohī naikṛtiko'nṛtī vā
pūrvāśī vā pitṛdevātithibhyaḥ ||
english: May there be none in our family who makes enmity, no king's minister who steals others' property, no betrayer of friends, no deceiver or liar, and none who eats before the ancestors, gods and guests.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यश्च नो ब्राह्मणं हन्याद्यश्च नो ब्राह्मणान्द्विषेत् ।
न नः स समितिं गच्छेद्यश्च नो निर्वपेत्कृषिम् ॥
iast:
yaśca no brāhmaṇaṃ hanyādyaśca no brāhmaṇāndviṣet |
na naḥ sa samitiṃ gacchedyaśca no nirvapetkṛṣim ||
english: Whoever among us kills a brahmin or hates brahmins, and whoever among us takes up farming, let him not come to our assembly.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
तृणानि भूमिरुदकं वाक्चतुर्थी च सूनृता ।
सतामेतानि गेहेषु नोच्छिद्यन्ते कदा चन ॥
iast:
tṛṇāni bhūmirudakaṃ vākcaturthī ca sūnṛtā |
satāmetāni geheṣu nocchidyante kadā cana ||
english: A grass mat, ground, water, and fourth, kind words: these are never lacking in the homes of the good.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
श्रद्धया परया राजन्नुपनीतानि सत्कृतिम् ।
प्रवृत्तानि महाप्राज्ञ धर्मिणां पुण्यकर्मणाम् ॥
iast:
śraddhayā parayā rājannupanītāni satkṛtim |
pravṛttāni mahāprājña dharmiṇāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām ||
english: These, king, offered with supreme faith as hospitality, are the practice of righteous people who do good deeds, very wise one.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सूक्ष्मोऽपि भारं नृपते स्यन्दनो वै
शक्तो वोढुं न तथान्ये महीजाः ।
एवं युक्ता भारसहा भवन्ति
महाकुलीना न तथान्ये मनुष्याः ॥
iast:
sūkṣmo'pi bhāraṃ nṛpate syandano vai
śakto voḍhuṃ na tathānye mahījāḥ |
evaṃ yuktā bhārasahā bhavanti
mahākulīnā na tathānye manuṣyāḥ ||
english: Even a small chariot, king, can bear a load that other things from the earth cannot. So people of great families, when joined to a task, bear the burden, and other people do not.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न तन्मित्रं यस्य कोपाद्बिभेति
यद्वा मित्रं शङ्कितेनोपचर्यम् ।
यस्मिन्मित्रे पितरीवाश्वसीत
तद्वै मित्रं सङ्गतानीतराणि ॥
iast:
na tanmitraṃ yasya kopādbibheti
yadvā mitraṃ śaṅkitenopacaryam |
yasminmitre pitarīvāśvasīta
tadvai mitraṃ saṅgatānītarāṇi ||
english: That is no friend whose anger one fears, or a friend who must be approached with suspicion. The friend in whom one can trust as in a father: that is a friend; the rest are mere acquaintances.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यदि चेदप्यसम्बन्धो मित्रभावेन वर्तते ।
स एव बन्धुस्तन्मित्रं सा गतिस्तत्परायणम् ॥
iast:
yadi cedapyasambandho mitrabhāvena vartate |
sa eva bandhustanmitraṃ sā gatistatparāyaṇam ||
english: Even if unrelated, one who acts in friendship is the true kinsman, the true friend, the refuge and the final support.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
चलचित्तस्य वै पुंसो वृद्धाननुपसेवतः ।
पारिप्लवमतेर्नित्यमध्रुवो मित्र सङ्ग्रहः ॥
iast:
calacittasya vai puṃso vṛddhānanupasevataḥ |
pāriplavamaternityamadhruvo mitra saṅgrahaḥ ||
english: For a person of fickle mind who does not serve the elders, whose thinking always wavers, the gathering of friends is never lasting.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
चलचित्तमनात्मानमिन्द्रियाणां वशानुगम् ।
अर्थाः समतिवर्तन्ते हंसाः शुष्कं सरो यथा ॥
iast:
calacittamanātmānamindriyāṇāṃ vaśānugam |
arthāḥ samativartante haṃsāḥ śuṣkaṃ saro yathā ||
english: Wealth passes by the fickle-minded, undisciplined person who follows the senses, as swans leave a dry lake.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अकस्मादेव कुप्यन्ति प्रसीदन्त्यनिमित्ततः ।
शीलमेतदसाधूनामभ्रं पारिप्लवं यथा ॥
iast:
akasmādeva kupyanti prasīdantyanimittataḥ |
śīlametadasādhūnāmabhraṃ pāriplavaṃ yathā ||
english: They grow angry for no reason and are pleased without cause: this is the character of the wicked, like a drifting cloud.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सत्कृताश्च कृतार्थाश्च मित्राणां न भवन्ति ये ।
तान्मृतानपि क्रव्यादाः कृतघ्नान्नोपभुञ्जते ॥
iast:
satkṛtāśca kṛtārthāśca mitrāṇāṃ na bhavanti ye |
tānmṛtānapi kravyādāḥ kṛtaghnānnopabhuñjate ||
english: Those who, honoured and helped by friends, do not stand by them: even flesh-eating creatures will not eat such ungrateful people when dead.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अर्थयेदेव मित्राणि सति वासति वा धने ।
नानर्थयन्विजानाति मित्राणां सारफल्गुताम् ॥
iast:
arthayedeva mitrāṇi sati vāsati vā dhane |
nānarthayanvijānāti mitrāṇāṃ sāraphalgutām ||
english: One should seek out friends whether one has wealth or not; without asking of them, one does not learn which friends are solid and which hollow.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते रूपं सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते बलम् ।
सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते ज्ञानं सन्तापाद्व्याधिमृच्छति ॥
iast:
santāpādbhraśyate rūpaṃ santāpādbhraśyate balam |
santāpādbhraśyate jñānaṃ santāpādvyādhimṛcchati ||
english: Through grief beauty is lost; through grief strength is lost; through grief knowledge is lost; through grief one falls ill.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अनवाप्यं च शोकेन शरीरं चोपतप्यते ।
अमित्राश्च प्रहृष्यन्ति मा स्म शोके मनः कृथाः ॥
iast:
anavāpyaṃ ca śokena śarīraṃ copatapyate |
amitrāśca prahṛṣyanti mā sma śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ ||
english: What is beyond reach is not gained by grieving; the body only suffers, and enemies rejoice. Do not set your mind on grief.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
पुनर्नरो म्रियते जायते च
पुनर्नरो हीयते वर्धते पुनः ।
पुनर्नरो याचति याच्यते च
पुनर्नरः शोचति शोच्यते पुनः ॥
iast:
punarnaro mriyate jāyate ca
punarnaro hīyate vardhate punaḥ |
punarnaro yācati yācyate ca
punarnaraḥ śocati śocyate punaḥ ||
english: Again and again a person dies and is born; again and again a person declines and grows; again and again a person begs and is begged from; again and again a person grieves and is grieved for.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सुखं च दुःखं च भवाभवौ च
लाभालाभौ मरणं जीवितं च ।
पर्यायशः सर्वमिह स्पृशन्ति
तस्माद्धीरो नैव हृष्येन्न शोचेत् ॥
iast:
sukhaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ ca bhavābhavau ca
lābhālābhau maraṇaṃ jīvitaṃ ca |
paryāyaśaḥ sarvamiha spṛśanti
tasmāddhīro naiva hṛṣyenna śocet ||
english: Pleasure and pain, rise and fall, gain and loss, death and life: all these touch everyone in turn. So the steady person neither exults nor grieves.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
चलानि हीमानि षडिन्द्रियाणि
तेषां यद्यद्वर्तते यत्र यत्र ।
ततस्ततः स्रवते बुद्धिरस्य
छिद्रोद कुम्भादिव नित्यमम्भः ॥
iast:
calāni hīmāni ṣaḍindriyāṇi
teṣāṃ yadyadvartate yatra yatra |
tatastataḥ sravate buddhirasya
chidroda kumbhādiva nityamambhaḥ ||
english: These six senses are restless. Wherever any of them goes, there a person's understanding flows out, like water from a cracked pot, constantly.

speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
तनुरुच्छः शिखी राजा मिथ्योपचरितो मया ।
मन्दानां मम पुत्राणां युद्धेनान्तं करिष्यति ॥
iast:
tanurucchaḥ śikhī rājā mithyopacarito mayā |
mandānāṃ mama putrāṇāṃ yuddhenāntaṃ kariṣyati ||
english: King Yudhishthira, like a slender flame, whom I treated falsely, will put an end to my foolish sons in war.

speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
नित्योद्विग्नमिदं सर्वं नित्योद्विग्नमिदं मनः ।
यत्तत्पदमनुद्विग्नं तन्मे वद महामते ॥
iast:
nityodvignamidaṃ sarvaṃ nityodvignamidaṃ manaḥ |
yattatpadamanudvignaṃ tanme vada mahāmate ||
english: All this is always anxious; this mind is always anxious. Tell me, very wise one, that state which is free of anxiety.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
नान्यत्र विद्या तपसोर्नान्यत्रेन्द्रिय निग्रहात् ।
नान्यत्र लोभसन्त्यागाच्छान्तिं पश्याम तेऽनघ ॥
iast:
nānyatra vidyā tapasornānyatrendriya nigrahāt |
nānyatra lobhasantyāgācchāntiṃ paśyāma te'nagha ||
english: I see no peace for you, sinless one, other than through learning and austerity, other than through restraint of the senses, other than through giving up greed.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
बुद्ध्या भयं प्रणुदति तपसा विन्दते महत् ।
गुरुशुश्रूषया ज्ञानं शान्तिं त्यागेन विन्दति ॥
iast:
buddhyā bhayaṃ praṇudati tapasā vindate mahat |
guruśuśrūṣayā jñānaṃ śāntiṃ tyāgena vindati ||
english: By understanding one drives away fear; by austerity one gains greatness; by serving the teacher one gains knowledge; by letting go one finds peace.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अनाश्रिता दानपुण्यं वेद पुण्यमनाश्रिताः ।
रागद्वेषविनिर्मुक्ता विचरन्तीह मोक्षिणः ॥
iast:
anāśritā dānapuṇyaṃ veda puṇyamanāśritāḥ |
rāgadveṣavinirmuktā vicarantīha mokṣiṇaḥ ||
english: Not depending on the merit of giving, not depending on the merit of the Veda, free of attraction and aversion, those who seek liberation move about here.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
स्वधीतस्य सुयुद्धस्य सुकृतस्य च कर्मणः ।
तपसश्च सुतप्तस्य तस्यान्ते सुखमेधते ॥
iast:
svadhītasya suyuddhasya sukṛtasya ca karmaṇaḥ |
tapasaśca sutaptasya tasyānte sukhamedhate ||
english: At the end of well-done study, a well-fought battle, a good deed and well-practised austerity, happiness grows.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
स्वास्तीर्णानि शयनानि प्रपन्ना
न वै भिन्ना जातु निद्रां लभन्ते ।
न स्त्रीषु राजन्रतिमाप्नुवन्ति
न मागधैः स्तूयमाना न सूतैः ॥
iast:
svāstīrṇāni śayanāni prapannā
na vai bhinnā jātu nidrāṃ labhante |
na strīṣu rājanratimāpnuvanti
na māgadhaiḥ stūyamānā na sūtaiḥ ||
english: Those who are divided never find sleep, even lying on well-spread beds; they find no joy in women, king, nor in being praised by bards and heralds.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न वै भिन्ना जातु चरन्ति धर्मं
न वै सुखं प्राप्नुवन्तीह भिन्नाः ।
न वै भिन्ना गौरवं मानयन्ति
न वै भिन्नाः प्रशमं रोचयन्ति ॥
iast:
na vai bhinnā jātu caranti dharmaṃ
na vai sukhaṃ prāpnuvantīha bhinnāḥ |
na vai bhinnā gauravaṃ mānayanti
na vai bhinnāḥ praśamaṃ rocayanti ||
english: The divided never practise dharma; the divided never find happiness here; the divided do not honour the worthy; the divided do not like peace.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न वै तेषां स्वदते पथ्यमुक्तं
योगक्षेमं कल्पते नोत तेषाम् ।
भिन्नानां वै मनुजेन्द्र परायणं
न विद्यते किं चिदन्यद्विनाशात् ॥
iast:
na vai teṣāṃ svadate pathyamuktaṃ
yogakṣemaṃ kalpate nota teṣām |
bhinnānāṃ vai manujendra parāyaṇaṃ
na vidyate kiṃ cidanyadvināśāt ||
english: Good advice does not please them, and their getting and keeping does not prosper. For the divided, lord of men, there is no end other than destruction.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सम्भाव्यं गोषु सम्पन्नं सम्भाव्यं ब्राह्मणे तपः ।
सम्भाव्यं स्त्रीषु चापल्यं सम्भाव्यं ज्ञातितो भयम् ॥
iast:
sambhāvyaṃ goṣu sampannaṃ sambhāvyaṃ brāhmaṇe tapaḥ |
sambhāvyaṃ strīṣu cāpalyaṃ sambhāvyaṃ jñātito bhayam ||
english: Wealth is to be expected in cows, austerity in a brahmin, fickleness in women, and danger from kin.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
तन्तवोऽप्यायता नित्यं तन्तवो बहुलाः समाः ।
बहून्बहुत्वादायासान्सहन्तीत्युपमा सताम् ॥
iast:
tantavo'pyāyatā nityaṃ tantavo bahulāḥ samāḥ |
bahūnbahutvādāyāsānsahantītyupamā satām ||
english: Threads, though thin, when always stretched together and many and equal, bear many strains because they are many: this is the image of the good.
